title: Successful catheter ablation of focal ventricular tachycardia originating from right bundle branch without making right bundle branch block, using pharmacologic induction by landiolol
case_prompt:
A 6-year-old girl was referred after school ECG screening revealed a ventricular tachycardia at 120 bpm.  
Her surface 12-lead ECG showed a competing narrow-QRS tachycardia at 100 bpm. Sinus rhythm QRS width was 72 ms with axis 92°; during VT the QRS was left bundle branch block type with inferior axis, width 92 ms, axis 58°. She was asymptomatic with normal cardiac structure and no tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy. VT was suppressed by exercise testing. A 24-hour Holter ECG showed heart rates of 85–169 bpm (average 106 bpm) with VT 55% of the time. Bisoprolol (0.1 mg/kg/day) reduced sinus rhythm but increased VT burden to 99%; the drug was discontinued.  
At age 8, she presented with sustained VT at 150 bpm with the same QRS morphology.  
An electrophysiology study under general anesthesia placed decapolar catheters in the right atrium, His position, and right ventricle. Atrial pacing at 120 ppm suppressed VT; it reappeared only after stopping pacing. Standard pacing maneuvers failed to induce VT. Intravenous landiolol (up to 6 μg/kg/min) converted sinus rhythm to VT at 100 bpm. During sinus rhythm, the His potential preceded QRS onset with a proximal-to-distal sequence and an H–V interval of 22 ms. During VT, the His potential preceded QRS onset with a distal-to-proximal sequence and an H–V interval of 12 ms.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Distinction from right ventricular outflow tract VT — “The QRS morphology of this tachycardia is left bundle branch block (LBBB) type, inferior axis, and wide QRS complex. In contrast, focal VT originating from the RBB (RBB-VT)... narrow QRS complex.”  
2. Exclusion of junctional rhythm with LBBB — “The junctional rhythm with LBBB usually has a normal H–V duration and His potential followed by RBB potential. However, these characteristics were not observed in our case.”  
3. Exclusion of bundle branch reentry — “The bundle branch reentry with RBBB has a prolonged H–V duration and His potential followed by RBB potential. However, these characteristics were not observed in our case.”  
4. Exclusion of Mahaim fiber automaticity — “In the Mahaim fiber automaticity, the earliest Mahaim potential is usually placed on the tricuspid annulus, and rapid atrial pacing reveals atriofascicular accessory pathway with decremental properties. However, these characteristics were not observed in our case.”
